mindBenders.subject: Physics
mindBenders.title: Can Acceleration Be Non-Zero When Velocity Is Exactly Zero?
mindBenders.teaser: Think of a ball thrown vertically upward at the very peak of its trajectory.
mindBenders.explanation: Yes! At the highest point, velocity momentarily passes through zero (v = 0), but the gravitational acceleration remains downward at g = 9.8 m/s². If acceleration were zero at the top, the ball would remain suspended in mid-air forever!

mindBenders.subject: Chemistry
mindBenders.title: Why Does Ice Spontaneously Melt at Room Temp Even Though Melting Is Endothermic?
mindBenders.teaser: ΔH is positive (heat is absorbed), so why does it happen spontaneously without driving it?
mindBenders.explanation: Because Gibbs energy ΔG = ΔH - TΔS! Liquid water has significantly higher entropy (randomness) than rigid ice (ΔS > 0). At T > 273.15 K, the TΔS term outweighs ΔH, making ΔG strictly negative and melting spontaneous.

mindBenders.subject: Mathematics
mindBenders.title: Why Is 0/0 Indeterminate While 0/5 is 0 and 5/0 is Undefined?
mindBenders.teaser: 0 divided by any number is 0, but any number divided by itself is 1. Which rule wins?
mindBenders.explanation: 0/0 is indeterminate because depending on the limiting rate at which the numerator and denominator approach zero, the limit can equal ANY real number! That's why we use algebraic factoring, rationalization, and standard limit theorems.

mindBenders.subject: Physics
mindBenders.title: Does Centrifugal Force Actually Exist in an Inertial Frame?
mindBenders.teaser: When you turn sharply in a car, you feel pushed outward. Is a real outward force acting on you?
mindBenders.explanation: No! From ground frame, only the centripetal inward force (friction/seatbelt) is real. The 'outward push' is your body's own inertia (Newton's 1st Law) wanting to continue in a straight line tangent to the circle. Centrifugal force is a pseudo-force used only in rotating non-inertial frames.

mindBenders.subject: Chemistry
mindBenders.title: Why Is the Electron Gain Enthalpy of Chlorine More Negative Than Fluorine?
mindBenders.teaser: Fluorine is the most electronegative element, so shouldn't it release the most energy when taking an electron?
mindBenders.explanation: Fluorine is extremely compact (2p subshell). Adding an electron causes intense inter-electronic repulsion in its tiny valence shell. Chlorine (3p subshell) is larger, so it accommodates the incoming electron with much lower repulsion, releasing more energy!
